newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mum on details of settlement report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mum on details of settlement report.

text.p: The United States acknowledged on Tuesday it recently completed a study of Israeli settlement activity but refused to confirm a published report that the study found more than a quarter of settler homes were empty.

"I can't speak specifically about this report because it has not been made public but we have from time to time and just recently tried to establish a basis of information for ourselves and for the Congress on this issue and we've done that," State Department Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Israel's Haaretz daily said Washington, citing U.S. data showing a large number of homes lying vacant, believed any expansion of Jewish settlements was unnecessary. The report has caused controversy in Israel where Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu dismissed it as groundless.

At a news briefing, Burns confirmed that legislation under which the United States provided Israel with housing loan guarantees imposed a responsibility on Washington to monitor settlement activity, including such factors as construction and occupancy. But "I can't speak about this (newspaper) report," he said.
Burns said he did not believe the issue came up in U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross' talks in the Middle East last week.
Later, a senior U.S. official who refused to speak on the record said: "I'm not sure about the full accuracy of this particular report in the Israeli press."
